candidates.title: Send an email when an app event occurs

demandEvidence.chore: Send an email when an app event occurs
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: I want a Make scenario to send an email through DigitalAka when a trigger occurs in another app.

ease.reason: A sample trigger and test email are easy to sketch, but no attached source documents an implementation capability.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: small professional service firms may pay to connect a trigger to email; the request proves no buyers or payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week mock can map one supplied event to a test email; live credentials, delivery and edge cases are untested.

autonomy.reason: A proposed trigger-to-email loop can repeat, but a person must configure access and verify every recipient and send.

evidence.reason: The request explicitly names triggered email through DigitalAka, but gives no frequency, fields or implementation evidence.

candidates.reason: Assessed a proposed event-to-test-email loop; mean 22/5 = 4.4, below 6. A single integration request does not establish repeat demand.

candidates.title: Review and enrich incoming leads

demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: An end-to-end autonomous Lead Qualification & CRM Enrichment workflow built in n8n.

ease.reason: A synthetic lead can be labeled and formatted for review, but no attached source documents enrichment or qualification capabilities.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: small professional service firms may pay for lead review assistance; the announcement establishes no buyers or payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week mock could classify supplied fictional leads, while criteria, data fields and enrichment access are unspecified.

autonomy.reason: A proposed label or summary might repeat, but a person must define rules, verify data and decide qualification.

evidence.reason: The post names lead qualification and CRM enrichment but supplies no workflow details, repeated need or implementation reference.

candidates.reason: Assessed a synthetic lead review experiment; mean 19/5 = 3.8, below 6. The announcement gives little workflow detail or evidence of customer demand.

rejected.title: A menu bar app brings the Dock to the pointer
rejected.reason: The only evidence is a Show HN title describing an app feature; it states no concrete chore, problem or request for a tool/service.

rejected.title: Pinterest publishing and analytics node
rejected.reason: The post describes capabilities of a node the author built, including scheduling and batch publishing, but states no concrete customer chore or request for service.

rejected.title: Send an email when an app event occurs
rejected.reason: Below threshold after assessing a narrow sample event-to-test-email experiment (mean 4.4/10); one request does not establish repeated demand and no implementation source is attached.

rejected.title: Consumer agent testing tool
rejected.reason: The announcement says its tool helps teams iterate against proprietary assistants, but gives no concrete task details or request. A separate test workflow and buyer need cannot be inferred.

rejected.title: Lead qualification and CRM enrichment workflow
rejected.reason: Below threshold after assessing a synthetic lead review experiment (mean 3.8/10); this announcement names a workflow but supplies no input, criteria, repeated demand or implementation reference.

rejected.title: Cloudflare R2 signer configuration
rejected.reason: This is a one-off technical support question about a signer configuration, not a repeated service chore; proposing an automated service would invent a recurring need.

steps.message: Assessed all six sealed discussion assignments. The two concrete proposed experiments scored below 6; the remaining four lack an eligible concrete chore or describe a one-off technical issue. No post proposed.
